question.text: A particle travels along a semicircular track having a radius of 1.0 m, starting at point A and reaching point B located at the opposite end of the diameter. If this motion takes a duration of 1.0 s, calculate the magnitude of the particle's average velocity.
conditions: points A and B are diametrically opposite ends of the path

figure.description: A semicircular path of radius 1.0 m connects starting position A at the top to final position B at the bottom along the circumference, with a straight vertical diameter of length 2.0 m joining A and B.

solution.approach: Average velocity depends only on the straight-line displacement between the start and end points, not on the curved path taken.

steps.text: Points A and B are the two ends of the vertical diameter of the semicircle.
The displacement from A to B is the diameter, twice the radius.
Divide the displacement by the time taken to get the average velocity.

common_mistakes.text: Using the curved arc length instead of the straight-line displacement gives π × 1.0 = 3.14 m/s, which is the average speed, not the average velocity.
